extracted.intended_audience: national IP offices, patent and trademark attorneys, policymakers, courts, licensees and other IP practitioners in Member States (utility models & trademarks)
extracted.subtask_description: Legal and procedural standards governing utility models (non-voluntary licenses, invalidity, enforcement, penalties, restoration, forfeiture) and trademark registration/rights under the Member States' implementing Annex (Bangui Agreement context).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable remuneration for non-voluntary licenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Remuneration for a non-voluntary license must be equitable, having due regard to all the circumstances of the case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remuneration may be subject to judicial revision on application by either the beneficiary of the non-voluntary license or the owner of the certificate of registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasoned judicial decision and registration
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision of the competent domestic court granting a non-voluntary license shall be reasoned and the final decision shall be transmitted to the Organization by the most diligent party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Organization shall enter the decision in the special register and notify it to any licensee whose name appears in the special register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of rights after grant of non-voluntary license
rubrics_metrics.description: After expiry of appeal time or after an appeal decision upholding the grant, the licensee is authorized to exploit the invention protected by the utility model according to the terms laid down in the court decision and must pay the remuneration specified therein.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of non-voluntary license on other licenses
rubrics_metrics.description: The grant of a non-voluntary license does not affect existing license contracts or non-voluntary licenses and does not preclude concluding other licenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, the owner may not grant other licensees terms more favourable than those of the non-voluntary license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on sublicensing and permitted transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: Beneficiary of a non-voluntary license may not, without the owner’s consent, grant third-party permission to perform acts authorized under the license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notwithstanding that restriction, a non-voluntary license may be transferred together with the goodwill/business working the invention, but only with authorization of the competent domestic court; the new beneficiary assumes the same obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of non-voluntary license decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The competent domestic court may amend the decision granting a non-voluntary license on application by the owner or beneficiary where new facts justify amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for withdrawal of non-voluntary license
rubrics_metrics.description: The court may withdraw a non-voluntary license on application by the owner if (a) grounds for grant have ceased, (b) beneficiary fails to comply with defined scope, or (c) beneficiary is in arrears with payment of compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In cases (a) and (b), withdrawal may be sought by other licensees; if withdrawal would cause serious adverse consequences for the beneficiary, a reasonable period to cease working may be allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of related provisions to amendment/withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions governing grant and management (Articles 39 and 40) apply to amendment or withdrawal of non-voluntary licenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal rights and suspensive effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner, beneficiary or any person who sought grant of non-voluntary license may, within one month of publication, appeal to the competent higher court against certain decisions; such appeals contesting grant, authorization to transfer, or amendment/withdrawal have suspensive effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions on appeal shall be notified to the Organization for entry in the special register and publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensee’s right to request enforcement action
rubrics_metrics.description: A beneficiary of a contractual or non-voluntary license may request the owner by registered letter to bring necessary judicial action for civil or criminal penalties for violations of rights under the certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If owner refuses or fails to institute action within three months, the registered licensee may institute the action in his own name, without prejudice to the owner’s right to intervene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discharge of obligations upon invalidation
rubrics_metrics.description: If a final judicial decision declares the certificate of registration invalid, the beneficiary of a non-voluntary license is discharged from all obligations resulting from the decision granting the license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-voluntary licenses in national interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a utility model is vital to national economy, public health, national defense, or its non-working/insufficient working has severe adverse effects, it may be subjected to a non-voluntary license by administrative order of the competent Minister.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The administrative act shall determine duration, scope (including importation), quantities, territory/region, and fees; licenses for health needs follow specified conditions; for anti-competitive practice or emergency no amicable agreement is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ministerial fixation and review of terms
rubrics_metrics.description: If no agreement is reached between owner and Ministry on duration/scope/fees of a non-voluntary license in national interest, the competent Minister may fix them on his authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These terms may be reviewed on application of the most diligent party.

rubrics_metrics.name: License as of right registration and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner may request that 'license as of right' be entered in the register for his certificate; the entry enables anyone to obtain a license under conditions fixed by court if no agreement, and entails reduction of annual fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner may request removal of indication; if removed and no license extant or by unanimous consent, Organization removes it on payment of fees that would have been due; beneficiaries of such license may not assign it or grant subsidiary licenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for invalidity of utility models
rubrics_metrics.description: Utility models shall be declared invalid if they (a) are not new, lack inventive step, or are not industrially applicable; (b) are not registrable under Article 4 (e.g., prohibited articles); or (c) the specification does not conform to required stipulations or fails to state true methods completely and truthfully.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invalidity may relate to all or some claims; certificates for improvements not connected with the utility model shall likewise be declared invalid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture for non-payment of annual fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner who has not paid annual fees on anniversary date forfeits all rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A six-month grace period is allowed during which payment (with an additional fee) is still valid; payments during grace are considered valid; similar rules apply for converted applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration after non-renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: Where protection lapsed due to circumstances beyond owner’s control, owner or entitled persons may apply for restoration by paying required annual fee and surcharge within six months of cessation and no later than two years from due date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application sent to Organization with statement of grounds; Organization may restore or reject; restoration does not extend maximum duration; rejection is appealable within 60 days; restored utility models shall be published; applies also where filing deadlines under international agreements were missed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standing and Public Prosecutor participation in invalidity/forfeiture actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions seeking invalidity or forfeiture may be brought by any person with standing; the Office of the Public Prosecutor may intervene, make submissions, or even directly initiate principal suit in specified cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All persons with rights entered in the special register shall be respondents when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competent court for invalidity/ownership disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions seeking invalidity, forfeiture or disputes relating to ownership shall be brought before competent domestic courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If action brought against owner and limited licensees simultaneously, it shall be brought before the court in the domicile of the owner; matters shall be investigated in summary proceedings and transmitted to Public Prosecutor if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of judicial decisions on invalidity/forfeiture in register
rubrics_metrics.description: Where absolute invalidity or forfeiture has been pronounced by a court decision that is res judicata, the competent court shall inform the Organization and the invalidity/forfeiture shall be entered in the special register and published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication follows the format specified for granted utility models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of counterfeiting
rubrics_metrics.description: Counterfeiting is any violation of the rights of the owner of a registered utility model, including manufacture, use, sale of stolen goods, offering for sale, or introduction into territory of infringing objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil and criminal liability for counterfeiting and injunctive relief
rubrics_metrics.description: Counterfeiting incurs civil and criminal liability; competent domestic court may issue injunctions to stop or prevent counterfeiting and award damages and other compensation under national law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensees who invited the owner to act and the owner declined may apply for injunctions; licensees and holders may be parties in proceedings to seek compensation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts prior to registration not prejudicial (with exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: Acts occurring prior to registration shall not be considered prejudicial to the rights of the owner and may not be invoked to justify conviction, except for acts subsequent to communication to the alleged counterfeiter of an official copy of the description attached to the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Urgent measures to prevent infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person with standing may make an urgent application to court seeking orders against alleged counterfeiters or intermediaries to prevent imminent infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court may order urgent measures ex parte where delay would cause irreparable harm; the court may order measures only if reasonably accessible evidence makes it likely rights are being infringed; measures may include prohibition of acts, guarantees, seizure or transfer of suspected infringing products; if measures ordered prior to merits proceedings, applicant must file proceedings within 10 days or measures may be cancelled upon defendant request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seizure procedure and security deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: Owners or exclusive right holders may approach judicial officers (including customs) to obtain a detailed inventory, with or without seizure, of objects claimed counterfeit; order made on application and presentation of the certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge may require a security deposit before seizure; deposit must be adequate but not deterrent; deposit always required of foreigners; person in possession must be given a copy of the order and proof of deposit or else risk invalidity and damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit to initiate merits proceedings after seizure
rubrics_metrics.description: If petitioner fails to institute criminal or civil proceedings within 10 days of the seizure/inventory, such seizure/inventory shall be void, without prejudice to damages claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court-ordered search for information
rubrics_metrics.description: Court may order disclosure of documentation or information held by defendant or others to determine origin and distribution networks of counterfeit products or processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents/information sought may include names/addresses of producers, manufacturers, distributors, suppliers, wholesalers/retailers, quantities produced/sold/received/ordered, and prices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of damages for counterfeiting
rubrics_metrics.description: Court shall determine damages by having regard to adverse financial effects (including loss of earnings), profit made by counterfeiter, and moral damage caused to the title owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customs border measures for suspected counterfeit goods
rubrics_metrics.description: On written application with documentary proof, customs administration may detain goods suspected to be counterfeit when conducting controls; public prosecutor, applicant and importer must be informed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detention lifted within 10 working days if applicant fails to provide proof of interim measures or court application plus guarantees; applicant may request customs to provide names/addresses; customs may detain proprio motu on prima facie evidence; liability for unjustified detention except where customs acted in good faith; after expiry of 10-day limit, owner/importer/recipient may, on payment of security deposit, suspend detention order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for counterfeiting
rubrics_metrics.description: Offence of counterfeiting punishable by imprisonment of one to three years and a fine of 3,000,000 to 15,000,000 CFA francs, or one of these penalties alone, without prejudice to civil damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggravating circumstances increasing penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: Penalties shall be doubled in event of recidivism or other aggravating circumstances: recidivism is a prior conviction within previous two years; penalties doubled if counterfeiter is a person who worked or was employed in owner’s workshops or was associated with a worker and thereby knew processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In latter case, the worker/employee may be prosecuted as accomplice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisions of Member State legislation regarding mitigating circumstances shall apply to counterfeiting offences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiation of criminal proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Criminal proceedings may be instituted concurrently by the Public Prosecutor’s Office and the prejudiced party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal court authority to rule on validity and ownership challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: When seized of a counterfeiting case, competent criminal court shall rule on any challenges by defendant regarding invalidity, expiry, or ownership of the utility model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional penalties and remedial measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Courts may order convicted counterfeiters to withdraw infringing objects from commercial circuits, order destruction at convict’s cost, and publicize the verdict (posting/publication); measures instituted at counterfeiter’s cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These measures are without prejudice to damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usurpation sanction
rubrics_metrics.description: Person improperly availing himself of the status of owner (by signs, advertisement, marks etc.) without being in possession of a valid certificate shall be punishable by a fine of 1,000,000 to 3,000,000 CFA francs, without prejudice to civil damages; recidivism doubles the fine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation period for civil and criminal actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Civil and criminal actions under this part are time-barred by three years from the acts which triggered them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional application of Annex provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Annex applies to applications for utility models filed as from date of entry into force, subject to rights acquired under prior Annex II; applications filed before entry remain subject to prior rules but exercise of rights from earlier grants is subject to this Annex subject to acquired rights; Annex II repealed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional character of trademarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademarks and service marks are optional, though Member States may exceptionally declare them compulsory for specified goods or services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signs that may constitute a mark
rubrics_metrics.description: Any visible or audible sign used or intended to be used and capable of distinguishing goods or services may be a trademark/service mark, including denominations (words, surnames, letters, numerals), figurative signs (drawings, logos, holograms), shapes (product/packaging), arrangements and colors, audible signs (sounds, musical phrases), audiovisual signs, and series of signs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collective and certification marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Collective marks consist of marks of products/services whose use conditions are set in approved rules and used only by officially recognized public enterprises, unions, associations or producer groups; collective certification marks are applied to products/services that by nature possess specified properties/qualities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use limited to entities with legal personality and official recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marks not eligible for registration
rubrics_metrics.description: A mark may not be registered if: (a) it is not distinctive (e.g., necessary/genetic designation of product); (b) identical or confusingly similar to an earlier registered mark; (c) contrary to public policy/morality/law; (d) liable to mislead about geographical origin, nature or characteristics; (e) reproduces state emblems/official signs without permission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to the mark determined by first filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Ownership of a mark belongs to the person who first deposited it; joint ownership allowed; exclusive ownership cannot be claimed by performing acts unless filed for registration as prescribed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of well-known marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner of a well-known mark within international conventions may apply to domestic court for invalidation of the effects of a confusing later filing on the territory of a Member State; such action may not be taken more than five years following the application date if the later application was filed in good faith.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights conferred by trademark registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration confers ownership of the mark for designated goods/services; it prohibits reproduction, use or affixing of the mark (even with descriptive additions) for identical goods, and prohibits suppression or modification of a properly affixed mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also prohibits reproduction/imitation for similar goods/services likely to create confusion unless authorized by the owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations to trademark rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered mark does not permit owner to prohibit third-party use in good faith of personal name, address, pseudonym, geographical name, or accurate indications of type/quality/quantity/destination/value/place/period of production for identification/information purposes provided such use is not misleading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration does not permit owner to prohibit use in relation to goods lawfully sold under the mark in a territory (exhaustion) provided goods are unchanged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint ownership governance for marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Joint owners may each use the mark (with fair compensation to non-using co-owners); any joint owner may institute counterfeit proceedings (notify others); non-exclusive licenses may be granted with compensation; exclusive license requires agreement of all or court leave; assignment and first-refusal rules, relinquishment procedures and registry effects are specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft license agreements must be notified; various time-limits for opposition, acquisition, price fixing by court, and relinquishment effects are prescribed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing requirements for trademark application
rubrics_metrics.description: Application filed with Organization or Ministry must contain: application addressed to Director-General, proof of fee payment, reproduction of the mark with exhaustive list of goods/services and corresponding Nice classes, regulations for collective marks if applicable, priority document if any, and unstamped private power of attorney if represented by an agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of trademark registration (Nice classification)
rubrics_metrics.description: A mark may be registered for one or more classes of goods and/or services as set forth in the Nice Agreement classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing report and transmittal of documents
rubrics_metrics.description: A report prepared by the Organization or Ministry shall note each filing and specify the date and time of submission; a copy of the report shall be issued to the applicant.
